messages.text: 0554, hub closed, 150 m vis, fog forecast to lift 0930. No diversions, 16 aircraft in, none airborne, 20 arrivals/hour on reopen, first landing FT 455 at 0930. No stuck guests. Holding plans.

Hub closed 05:54, visibility 150 m, fog forecast to lift 09:30, no diversions or stuck guests. Duty risk: C07 out of duty at 07:37, C15 at 08:00 — they may time out before reopening. Options at 09:30 will be framed for approval.
Diversions: 2 flights at DWC with 574 guests, 1 at SHJ with 312; 1066 guests stuck total. I'll start rebooking, meals and hotel planning for both sites.
Diversions: 2 flights/574 guests at DWC, 1 flight/312 at SHJ, 1066 total. FT 402 09:33, FT 064 09:42, FT 918 09:36 on reopen; need guest recovery plan for 1066.

Three diversions: 2 flights at DWC with 574 guests, 1 at SHJ with 312 — 1066 guests stuck total. Hub still closed, fog lifting 09:30. I've flagged the duty manager and will work rebooking, meals and hotels.
Handed guest-recovery the 1,066-guest picture. I'll keep tracking the diverted aircraft's return slots as reopen plans firm up.
Current picture shows a third diversion at AAN with 184 guests, total stuck 1430 — please extend rebooking, meals and hotel planning to AAN and proceed at all three sites.
Situational update at 06:12 shows one more diversion: AAN with 184 guests, total 1430, not 1066. Proceeding with rebooking, meals and hotels at all three sites.
C07 at DWC times out 07:37 with 61 min left, before 09:30 reopen — needs standby cover (S1/S2/S3 at HUB) or duty extension; also watch C15 (84 min, 08:00) and C10 at SHJ (99 min, 08:15).
Flagged C07 at DWC (61 min left, out 07:37, pre-reopen), C15 at HUB (84 min) and C10 at SHJ (99 min). Cover available: standbys S1–S3 at HUB with 564–594 min. Handing C07's cover to crew hotline.

C07 out 07:37 at DWC: HUB–DWC road is 76 min, so standby must roll immediately to make 09:30, else request duty extension. S1/S2 (560 min) or S3 (590) available at HUB. Also tracking C15 (80 min, out 08:00) and C10 at SHJ.
C07 can't make a 09:30 reopen unless a standby rolls now — the HUB–DWC drive is 76 min. S1, S2 and S3 are all legal at HUB; flagged the timing and extension option to Crew Control.
Crews confirm: C07 at DWC has 46 min left (out 07:37), C15 is at DWC (69 min, out 08:00) not HUB, C10 at SHJ 84 min. Road to DWC is 76 min, so C07 needs a duty extension now.
Crews confirm C07 is down to 46 min at DWC, C15 is at DWC (69 min, out 08:00), C10 at SHJ 84 min. Road time beats C07's clock, so passed a duty-extension request to Crew Control.
C07 at DWC (46 min left, out 07:37) needs duty extension now — 76-min road means standby can't make 09:30. C15 at DWC has 69 min, C10 at SHJ 84; please approve extensions.

C07 confirmed at 46 min, out 07:37 — can't make a 09:30 reopen with the 76-min road, so duty extension is the fix. Requested it from the duty manager, and flagged C15 (69 min, also DWC) and C10 (84 min, SHJ) for the same watch.
Approval framing: C07 (40 min) and C15 (63) at DWC need duty extensions for 09:30 reopen; road 76 min beats both. C10 at SHJ 78 min — confirm extension need before filing.
Confirmed: C10 (78 min, out 08:15) needs an extension too — SHJ road is 125 min, standby can't make 09:30. Please file duty extensions for C07, C15 and C10.
Confirming: C10 (78 min, out 08:15) needs an extension too — 125-min SHJ road beats its clock. All three (C07 40, C15 63, C10 78) filed for duty extensions to cover the 09:30 reopen.
Best for schedule: 15 of 16 aircraft home by 12:00, lowest 225-min delay. Risk: fog convoy to DWC/SHJ; one crew still times out.
B relieves C07, C15, C10 with standby buses before clocks run out; A times out four crews who can't legally extend. Risk: buses drive through 150 m fog — convoy, low speed, stand down if it thickens.
All three standbys legal with 542-572 min; B avoids four out-of-base duty expiries and fewest stranded guests. Risk: 150 m fog road convoy — low speed, stand down if it thickens.
Lowest harm (280 vs 1,091), cheapest at 1.42m, 15 home by 12:00; risk: fog convoy and one crew timing out.
Best for stranded crowds: 11,602 guest-hours and 4.7 h worst wait. Risk: 3 buses drive in 150 m fog — enforce convoy, low speed, stand down if thickens.
B cuts stranded guests from 1,091 to 280; best care outcome. Risk: fog convoy may stand down, so prep hotels/meals for a fallback to A.
B cuts stranded terminal crowds to 11,602 guest-hours, 4.7 h worst wait; I keep stands and gates ready for 09:30 reopen. Risk: fog convoy may slow — but stand-down protocol covers it.
B cuts stranded guests 1,091 to 280, cuts wait to 4.7h; under GCAA care fewer hotel/meals owed. Risk: fog stand-down mid-transit — I need fallback A hotel capacity staged now.
Keeping B: lowest harm 280 vs 1,091, cheapest 1.42m, 15 home by 12:00. Main risk: fog stand-down mid-convoy; Crew Hotline is right to demand hotel/meal fallback readiness.
Best punctuality: 225-min delays, 15 of 16 aircraft home by 12:00. If fog stops the convoy we lose crew relief; one crew still times out.
Standbys legal 542-572 min; buses relieve C07/C15/C10 before expiry. Risk: fog convoy stand-down strands relief — prep extensions/hotels fallback.
B saves C07, C15, C10 duty clocks; but one crew still times out, so hotels/rest now and convoy stand-down fallback prepared.

Recommendation to approver: Plan B — safety-gate passed, weighted score 74 vs A 20, cuts stranded guests to 280, saves 1.42m, gets 15 of 16 aircraft home by 12:00 — with the safety warning that the 150 m fog bus convoy must enforce low speed and stand down if it thickens, with hotels and meals staged for a fallback to Plan A.
Plan B approved: please confirm hotel and meal capacity staged now in case the fog convoy stands down mid-transit.

Plan B buses rolling: S1/S2 to DWC 76 min, S3 to SHJ 125 min. C07 (38 min left, out 07:37) and C15 (61 min) are caution — relief must arrive before expiry; C10 next tightest. Standbys legal 541–571 min, then fly FT 721/006/610 landing 09:30–09:39.

Plan B approved: stranded guests cut from 1,091 to 280, worst wait 4.7 h, 15 of 16 aircraft home by 12:00. Asked Hub Control to stage hotel and meal fallback capacity in case the fog convoy stands down.

Guests at diversions: DWC 1,795, SHJ 870, AAN 622, BAH 518 — 5,425 stuck total. With reopen 09:30, I'll propose water/food and welfare at each airport now, plus the hotel fallback hub-side if fog stands the convoy down.
C07 (10 min), C15 (33 min), C10 (48 min) need buses dispatched immediately; C12 BAH and C04/C09 AAN need road timings next.
Crews at DWC (C07 10 min, C15 33), SHJ (C10 48) need buses rolling now; C12 BAH, C04/C09 AAN and C03/C01 have 103–208 min. Told Crew Control.
C07 7 min, C15 30, C10 45 — relief must beat those clocks. C12 BAH has 100 min but no road link, needs positioning flight. C04/C09 AAN: road 97 min vs 180/205 min duty, legal.
Relief clocks tightening: C07 7 min, C15 30, C10 45. C12 BAH has 100 min but no road — needs positioning. C04/C09 AAN legal: 97-min road vs 180/205 min duty. Hotline updated.
C07/C15/C10 timed out; relief crews must fly their aircraft. C12 BAH only 54 min left and no road — needs positioning flight now. All other diversion crews legal 134–234 min.

C07, C15, C10 are timed out — their aircraft need the standby-relief crews. All AAN crews and SHJ C03/C06/C14 are legal; C12 at BAH is at 54 minutes with no road link and needs a positioning flight urgently.

Understood C07/C15/C10 timed out — relief must fly the aircraft. For C12 BAH (54 min, no road), FT 893's BAH fresh crew is the positioning option; suggest they check that pair. All other diversion crews 134–234 min legal — hotline confirms.

C07/C15/C10 logged as timed out — relief crews must fly the aircraft. For C12 BAH (54 min left, no road), the FT 893 fresh crew departing BAH 11:15 is the positioning option. Other crews legal at 134–234 min; hotline confirms.
Reopen 09:30: first arrivals FT 721 09:30, FT 006 09:33, FT 455 09:36; 16 aircraft inbound at ~20/hr. Stage gates and guest flow from 09:30, FT 893 lands 12:30.
Reopen 09:30: first arrivals FT 721 09:30, FT 006 09:33, FT 455 09:36, FT 610 09:39 — hub stands and turnaround ready for 20 arrivals/hour.

Recovery wave is rolling: first arrivals FT 721 09:30, FT 006 09:33, FT 455 09:36 — about 20 landings per hour, 16 aircraft total. Hub Control told to stage gates and guest flow from 09:30; FT 893's fresh crew departs BAH 11:15, lands 12:30.

Confirmed, hold the 09:30 plan: stands and turnaround ready for 20/hr, first arrivals 721/006/455/610. Crew Control is matching relief crews to inbound aircraft, including the FT 893 BAH positioning pair for C12.

Hub Control, your 09:30 reopen plan is confirmed — stands and turnaround ready for 20 arrivals/hour. Crew Control is matching relief crews to inbound aircraft, including the FT 893 BAH pair for the tight C12.

Recovery rolling: 6 of 16 landed, 9 in the air landing 09:48–10:18. One aircraft still waiting on a fresh crew — FT 893 at BAH, covered by the positioning pair departing 11:15, landing 12:30. 4,395 guests still to move.
Hotline report 10:16: 1716 guests stuck (280 at BAH); C12 BAH now timed out — confirm FT 893 positioning pair departing 11:15, landing 12:30 covers its aircraft.

Hotline report 10:16: 1,716 guests still stuck, 280 of them at BAH with the one diverted flight there. Only crew away is C12 at BAH, now timed out — the FT 893 positioning pair departing 11:15 lands 12:30; Crew Control notified.

Guest update: 1,716 guests still stuck, 280 of them at BAH with FT 893 (fresh crew departs 11:15, lands 12:30). FT 559 with C16 lands 10:18; recovery at 20 arrivals/hour — rebooking, meals and hotels staged as gates reopen.
Confirmed: FT 893 positioning pair departing BAH 11:15, landing 12:30 is the only relief needed and covers C12's timed-out aircraft; recovery now shows 1505 guests still stuck.
Confirmed — FT 893's positioning pair (departs BAH 11:15, lands 12:30) is the only crew still needed and covers C12's timed-out aircraft. Recovery now shows 1505 guests stuck, down from 1716.
Eight operating crews (C07/C15/C10/C12/C04/C03/C01/C09) are timed out; standby S1 and S2 at hub are legal with 299 minutes each — request approval to use them for relief swaps on inbound aircraft.

One aircraft still needs a fresh crew: FT 893 at BAH — its positioning pair departs 11:15, lands 12:30, so it's covered. Eight operating crews are timed out; S1/S2 have 299 minutes each, flagged to Hub Control.

Crew Control requests approval to use standbys S1 and S2 (299 minutes each) for relief swaps on timed-out crews C07/C15/C10/C12/C04/C03/C01/C09 — your approval needed; hub stands ready for the 09:30 wave.

Standby approval isn't mine to grant — passed the S1/S2 request (299 minutes each, for the eight timed-out crews) to the Duty Manager for decision. Hub stays ready for the 09:30 wave at 20 arrivals per hour.

For the approver: 15 of 16 aircraft home or inbound by 10:18; FT 893 at BAH is crewed via the 11:15/12:30 positioning pair. Guests stuck down to 1,505. Open item: eight timed-out crews; Crew Control requests standby S1/S2 (299 min each) for relief swaps — approval is yours, not mine. Lesson: position relief crews before duty timeouts hit, not after.

A.warning: 4 crews time out away from base: any request to extend duty must be refused.

B.warning: Buses drive out through fog (visibility 150 m): convoy, low speed, stand down if it thickens. 1 crew time out away from base: any request to extend duty must be refused.

verdict.reason: All 3 plans pass the safety gate. Weighted score: B 74, A 20, C 7. B leads on security, passengers, punctuality, environment, cost, schedule.
